utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Madam Registrar and good afternoon, everybody. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci. I notice that all the accused are present. From the Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Krgovic and Mr. Ostojic. That's about it. Prosecution I notice the presence of Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. I understand there is some preliminary. Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, everyone. Could we go into private session just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course. Let's go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before I give you the floor, Mr. McCloskey, we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. Judge Stole, although he was here this morning, is not feeling well at all and he has asked me to relieve him. So he hopes to be able to join us tomorrow. That's number 1. Number 2, yesterday, you know that we had this inconvenient power outage. We convened you all here for a short while at 5.00. We were under the impression that the sitting was not being recorded. It now transpires that it was recorded and since it seems that it was not transmitted due to having been considered to be in closed session, when it shouldn't, and we wouldn't have conducted it in closed session, we are just declaring that it should be considered to be a sitting held in open, public session, and not in closed session. So it should be made available to whoever requires a transcript thereof. Having said that, let's go back to private session for a while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to raise the issue of disclosing of information report from June 2000 as to Prosecution Witness 109. He is scheduled to testify here with a conference link on this Friday and I got information report in a redacted form from the Prosecution. I'd ask them to provide me with an unredacted form of this report, and this morning, they refused to do that. I was notified that the redactions are related to the address and some contact details of the witness but I see from the same report that the witness refused to give any address or contact details, so I need this report in unredacted form so -- for proper preparation of my cross-examination, and I'd ask the Chamber to order the Prosecution to disclose this information report in its entirety without redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking of Witness PW-109. That's his, nom de plume, his pseudonym. Who is going to respond to that? Mr. Thayer? I suggest you first give information as to what the redacted parts actually refer to and then respond to the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Just to be on the safe side, if we could move into closed session or private session for this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Gospodin Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal. You're about to start giving the evidence that you would have started giving yesterday. Unfortunately you know what happened. We had a power outage. I'm sure that was explained to you and that's why your testimony has been delayed for today. I'm sorry for that but it was beyond our control. Before you start your testimony, you are bound by our rules to make a solemn declaration that you will be testifying the truth. The text of the solemn declaration is being handed to you now. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Please make yourself comfortable. Now, Mr. Lazarevic, you are here to testify on certain events that the Prosecution alleges to have taken place in July of 1995. You will be asked questions by the -- Mr. Thayer for the Prosecution and then by the various Defence teams, but before Mr. Thayer starts with his questions, I need to explain to you or caution you on a right that you enjoy under our rules. It is being suggested or alleged that you were -- you lived through some of the events that are alleged by the Prosecution, and it is not to be excluded that questions could be put to you by either Mr. Thayer or by any of the Defence teams which, if you answer truthfully, could tend to incriminate you. I am not telling you that there will be such questions but just in case such questions are put to you, then you can -- you have a right to ask the three of us up here to exempt you from answering such questions. We have a choice. After hearing you, we can decide to exempt you from answering such questions or alternatively, we can decide that in the best interests of justice, we will compel you to answer such questions. So this right is limited and it is not an absolute one. However, in case such questions are asked and we compel you notwithstanding your request to answer such questions, then whatever evidence you give in answering such questions, unless it is false evidence, cannot be used against you in any subsequent criminal proceedings. Is that clear enough to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And were you alerted to this before you came into this room to testify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was indeed. I was prepared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. And that clears the way for the first question from -- by Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name for the record?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Damjan Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how old are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where were you born and raised?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In Celopek, near Zvornik, and I currently reside in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you identify yourself as a Bosnian Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I just want to ask you a couple of questions about your military service history. It will just take a moment. But please correct me when I'm done if I've gotten anything wrong or you need to clarify anything. When the Zvornik Brigade was formed, you began serving in the road and bridges platoon of the Zvornik Brigade's Engineering Company; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you served in the Engineering Company until shortly after the Dayton Accords or agreement was signed, is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, prior to serving in the Zvornik Brigade, can you just describe for the Trial Chamber, please, what your military service was from the beginning of the war up until that time?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, before the war I worked in a company, and when the war broke out, we were all mobilised. I was on the front line for some two months or so. And when the Engineering Company in the Zvornik Brigade was established, I was assigned to that brigade because when I served in the army, I was in charge of roads and bridges in the Engineering Company. That was my duty in the former army. And that's why I was assigned to the newly established engineers' company in the rear of the brigade where I was in charge of building roads, bridges and similar things.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Just one final question on your military service history. After the war broke out but before the formation of the Zvornik Brigade, did you serve in a TO or local unit of some sort at the front lines?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Before the conflicts broke out? No. I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. After the conflict broke out but before the establishment of the Zvornik Brigade, did you serve with -- in a local unit by the name of the Celopek unit? Because everybody in the unit was from the area of Celopek?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the Celopek Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to turn your attention, sir, to 1995 and specifically to the time period of July of 1995. The Zvornik Brigade itself was headquartered in some facilities that we have been referring to as Standard. But where was your Engineering Company itself headquartered?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the beginning, we were at the Standard, at the command, and then we separated and we had our premises in the so-called youth neighbourhood or youth area. That's what the youth brigades had built before the war, and that's where we were located after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in close proximity to this area where your engineering command was headquartered, were there also some companies or factories or other businesses located close by?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Around our premises, there were companies. For example, Glinica, the metalworks called Univerzal, and in the broader area, there were some other companies. The two that I've mentioned were the closest to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was the Glinica facility or factory also known to you by any other names?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Birac Holding, the company Glinica of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber how your Engineering Company was structured? For example, who was the chief of your company?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Major Jokic, Major Jokic. He was the chief of engineers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall his first name, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Jokic, Major Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who served directly under him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before you answer. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'd just like my colleague to clarify because he started his question and I referred to page 12-- sorry, to page 12, lines 10, when my colleague is asking how the engineering is -- company is structured, and then he follows with a question about the chief of engineering. The two are separate and I think my colleague should clarify that before asking questions to the witness. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right. Could you comply, please, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I think the next couple of questions, at least I hoped, would clarify that points which is obviously one that's important and we have alluded to that before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, both of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, with respect to your Engineering Company, from your experience and your recollection, in terms of the chain of command that operated at your company, who was directly below Chief Jokic in that chain of command as it related to your company?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean at the moment when the conflict broke out or maybe later?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Again, sir, I'm focusing on July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Jevtic. He was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you distinguish for the Trial Chamber what the difference was between the roles and responsibilities of the chief of engineering, Major Jokic, and Mr. Jevtic? If you know, if you recall.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The chief of engineers was superior to all of us in the company, and all the orders and tasks we received in the company, we received from him. Actually, the company commander received those and distributed them down the line to various parts of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall where Mr. Jokic, Dragan Jokic, had his office? Was it at your company command near the youth settlement or was his office at Standard in the brigade barracks?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that he had his office in -- down there in the Standard, but he was very much present in our headquarters. Whenever we -- he had time he would be with us, with our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, below Mr. Jevtic, who was next in line in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The deputy commander of our company was Slavko Bogicevic and he also acted as the chief of morale, guidance but he was also the deputy commander of the company, Slavko Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was there also a company clerk of some kind in your Engineering Company?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. He was the one who was acting as the deputy commander, and the officer for morale. He drafted daily orders and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember an individual by the name of Sekonjic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Vojkan Sekonjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was the company officer, the company desk officer, in our company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you explain what his role and responsibilities were, to the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He would draft the daily orders. He would also take attendance. He would be the one to record who was absent, who was present, in the unit on what day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just a couple more questions about the structure and then we'll move on to a different area, sir. Was your company divided into platoons and if so, would you describe how many and what they were called?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First we have the Pioneer Platoon; the second platoon was the platoon for roads and bridges; and the third platoon was the platoon for engineering works.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, in July of 1995, did you have any particular position within any of these platoons?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was the commander of the Roads and Bridges Platoon, which means that throughout the conflict I was in charge of building roads and bridges. This is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in July of 1995, did you have a particular rank, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was the sergeant second class. This is the rank that I obtained from the former army, and then, after different manoeuvres that I attended, I got the rank of a staff sergeant. And that was my rank at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how many men were in your platoon?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 10 to 12, maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And who was your immediate superior? I know you've given us the structure but when you were the -- in charge of that platoon, who was your immediate superior? To whom would you report directly?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, would you describe for the Trial Chamber, please, how your company typically received its tasks? How would orders typically flow through or flow into and through your company?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Every morning there was a briefing. The major would go to the brigade command. He would attend those briefings. And after the briefings ended, he would either come to us or he would call the company commander or his deputy on the phone and tell them what to do and what we were supposed to do. He would receive his tasks from the command and then he would convey those tasks either directly in person verbally or over the phone. He would tell us what to do and who was supposed to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, you referred to the major. You're referring, I take it, to Major Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What kind of construction equipment or heavy machinery did your platoon have itself in July of 1995? As opposed, for example, available to it from outside?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We did not have much, maybe two or three lorries and a 75 bulldozer, a Skip, which was a very small building machine, like a tractor with a bucket, and also had the digging part in the rear. It was a small machine that was not capable of engaging in any major construction works.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to take a couple of moments with you to talk about some specific pieces of machinery. So let's just take them one at a time and I'm going to ask you some questions about each one. You mentioned bulldozers, specifically I think you mentioned a 75 bulldozer. The -- that piece of machinery, was it referred to by any particular name or nickname?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a bulldozer, a 75, a Caterpillar machine. That machine had caterpillars.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you ever refer to it as just simply a Dozer or Dozer 75?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Dozer, bulldozer. Those were the names, the two names.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you described somewhat what a Skip is. Can you try to describe it in just a little bit more detail for us, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A Skip? A Skip is a machine which can be used in construction, in front it had a loading and unloading bucket, a small bucket, and in the back it had a backhoe for digging canals, trenches, that bucket is somewhat smaller, the one in the back. And the machine itself is somewhat smaller. It's a small building machine, a small construction machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it wheeled or is it on tracks?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Wheeled.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And I want to use a specific term that comes up from time to time. I don't mean to injure your language but have you heard the term "Rovokopac" or "Kopac" and if so, what does it refer to?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Many people call this thing Rovokopac. This is a machine that digs holes. You can use it in the construction industry, in private life, for bigger-scale works, for smaller-scale works.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to larger jobs and larger machinery that are required for those jobs, did your company itself have larger Rovokopacs, for example, or did you have to obtain them elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We did not have any larger machinery. Whenever the brigade needed something larger, then we would requisition such machinery from various construction companies that had them, backhoe excavators, loading machinery and staff. It all depended on what various companies had at their disposal and that we needed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I want to turn your attention specifically to a series of days that my friends and I all know that you're here to talk about. Would you please tell the Trial Chamber whether you recall receiving an order on a particular day in July of 1995 to go somewhere? And if so, please tell the Trial Chamber what that order entailed.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th June, I accompanied my son, who was going to the army, I was below the Standard with my son. My son was on his way to the army. I went home and on the following day, when I returned to the unit, I was given the task to go to Orahovac. When I asked why, they said, It is for you to go and for us to know. Trenches are being dug over there. You have to do something and you have to go. That's how I went. I had to go. I didn't have a choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just stop you right there, sir. In your answer, and I'm just referring to the transcript here, page 18, line 10, you referred to the 14th of June of 1995. And I'm asking you about specific events that occurred in July of 1995 and I just want to clarify the date and the month that we are talking about here, of these events.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I misspoke. I know what you're saying. I gave you the wrong month.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. So we are talking about being with your son on the 14th of July 1995; is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us that you received this order the next day, which would be the 15th of July. Would you please take the Trial Chamber through the events of that day, from the very beginning, and let's just start with where did you receive this order and from whom?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I got that order at the command -- at the company. Major Jokic was not there but Slavko Bogicevic was and some others and Major Jokic called and I was immediately sent up there to do whatever was being done there. I had to go. And when I arrived there, actually on my way up there, I came by a group of soldiers, somewhere around the school. There were a few of them there. I don't know the exact number. And there was some two or three soldiers with white belts. I proceeded to a well by the road leading to Krizevici. When I arrived there, on the right-hand side, I saw some meadows and a group of people or young men in that meadow. They had been dead. They had been killed. And I was told that there is a machine up there towards the flyover that had left on the 14th and that was already digging the graves. I went up there and below the fly bridge I did get a glimpse of the situation. I could not go any closer. I couldn't -- I couldn't stand the sight, and I returned. There were other people who were doing that. I returned on to the road, and then I returned to the base, and then I went home.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. I'm going to take you back a little bit and ask you for some more details about this day that you've just described. That morning, on the 15th of July, when you arrived at the company command, did you encounter any company soldiers talking amongst themselves about anything?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the entrance towards the barracks, there was a group of soldiers from a unit. They were discussing Orahovac. They said there were some people up there that should be buried. I didn't pay much heed to it and I went to the office where Slavko was, as well as Sekonjic and the rest. I was told that I should go up there as soon as possible to do that. I asked, "Why me?" And they said, "Well, it's you. Just go up there. You've got nothing to do with it but you just need to be there. You can say that your machine broke down and that you couldn't have done any work today." But however, it wasn't possible for me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, these soldiers who were talking amongst themselves, were they Engineering Company soldiers, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, our soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And you said that they were discussing Orahovac and that there were some people up there that should be buried. Did you overhear them saying anything about how those individuals died? Whether they were killed in battle or whether they were killed some other way, under some other circumstances?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't hear anything from them about how they died. I just heard that they said that there were people up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You told us that you left the compound. Were you told exactly where to go?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you told to go any place in particular in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From the place where the school is towards the Krizevici road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you go alone, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A vehicle brought me as far as the school, and then I continued on foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you arrived at the school, you said you saw some soldiers and some men in white belts. Do the white belts mean anything to you in terms of what the position or role of that individual is?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the only ones who had white belts were the military police in our brigade. No one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the school, how did you get to this other location that you described that was near a water source or a water point and the railroad tracks?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first location was next to the water point, in the meadow there. The other one was just below the tracks, somewhat further up. I went there on foot. I went on foot from the school to that location after I had come out of the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What was your specific assignment that morning, as it was relayed to you by Mr. Bogicevic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That I should go up there. He said, "A machine is already up there and you report there, see to it that they are buried." That is why I went there. As I said, I saw something under the overpass and returned after that. I saw some people working there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you arrived at the school, were you told anything about any machinery that was already present in the area working?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the base I was told that the machine had already gone up there with the engineers. After that, once I got there, no one told me anything. I wasn't down there by the soldiers next to the road. I went on after I passed the school and to the location itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, when you arrived at the school, how did you know where to go? How did you know where to report?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the base, I was told to follow the road to Krizevici. It passes by the school. That's the main road to Krizevici. And they said, "Well, next to the road you'll see where the location is. Just keep going."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately what time of the day it was when you arrived at the school?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was this in the evening, sir, or in the morning?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. When you arrived at the school in the morning, do you recall seeing any VRS officers from any brigade, from the corps, from the Main Staff, in the area of the school?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. When we passed by in that vehicle, I saw a few of those soldiers before the school. As for any officers, I didn't see any, be it at the school or at the location itself where the thing was being done.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: After you walked to this other site, along the road to the area where the water source was, can you describe in more detail what you saw?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The water point was the first location next to the road. The other one is further up next to the overpass. I saw some killed soldiers and civilians. I continued all the way up to the overpass. To the right-hand side, I could see one part of it and then I returned and went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: This first group of dead people, sir, you described as killed soldiers and civilians. Why do you say that they were soldiers and civilians?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because I noticed that a few of them had camouflage uniforms on. I presumed they were members of an army. And there were also civilians wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you estimate approximately how large this group of bodies was?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. There was a pile, a heap. I cannot tell you exactly. Well, a group of them, around 20, 25, 30. I can't say. I can't provide a figure. They were lying on top of each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you continued walking, you've described a railroad track. Is that railroad track on the ground, or is it elevated, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is elevated. That is the overpass across which the railroad tracks pass on, go on to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how far did you continue along that road leading towards the railroad tracks?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's not much of a distance, perhaps 150 or 200 metres, between the first and the second location, that is. That is my assessment. As to whether there was more or less, well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, where did you stop, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First I stopped just before the overpass. I was standing there for a short while thinking whether I should continue or not. And then once I passed the overpass, to my right-hand side I could see a few corpses right nearby, to the right side of the overpass, perhaps some 20 or 30 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you just mentioned seeing a few corpses as you were standing near the overpass. Can you estimate for the Trial Chamber, thinking back on that day as you saw what you saw from your location, how many corpses approximately did you see at that second location?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A larger number. They were somewhat dispersed. They were not in a pile. They covered a distance across the meadow. I don't know how many. I didn't come close. I could see from afar that that group was larger than the first group at the first location.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And from your position near these railroad tracks, were you able to see any machinery at work?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There was a machine, the BGH. It is a backhoe/excavator. It was sent there on the 14th. I don't know who sent it up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this BGH, do you recall whether the one you saw had a particular model number attached to it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: BGH, I think it was a BGH-500.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe the size and what this BGH machine looked like, for the Trial Chamber, please, just generally speaking, what's its design?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a construction machine used to dig canals, building foundations. At the front it has a bucket. It is a tracked vehicle. It can turn in any direction. It is a construction machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does BGH also make a 700 model, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any specific recollection as to whether this machine that you saw on that day was a BGH-500 -- I note that you say "I think it was a BGH-500" -- or a BGH-700?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, what should I tell you? I didn't pay any particular attention as to the number but I do think it was a 500 one, the smaller one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And are both of these models larger than the Engineering Company had in its own inventory at the compound?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: While you were in this area that day, did any other equipment arrive?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There was another ULT 220 that came. It was the property of the Birac Holding of the aluminum oxide factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this ULT 220, what kinds of machine is it? What does it do? And if you could describe what it looks like, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a self-propelled construction machine with wheels. In the front it has a loading bucket.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And as opposed to the Rovokopac type of machinery, such as the BGH-500, what is the ULT 220 designed to do? You've told us that the BGH is designed to dig trenches with its bucket. What is a ULT 220 primarily designed to do, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is mainly used to load construction material. That's its principal purpose. But it can also be used for smaller excavations on flat areas, but it cannot dig deeply.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer, by any chance, do you have perhaps photos of all these machines which we could show to the witness and also to us and it would make everybody's life much easier?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour, I do. I can show them now or I can wait until a little later but if Your Honour wishes I can do it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it will speed up and facilitate the whole --

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we may have 65 ter 2069 on e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, unfortunately this is the best photograph we have. Do you see an image on your -- in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is an excavator, a BGH-500.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And it is the machine that is directly in the centre of the photograph, correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The machinery next to the person in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is this the piece of machinery you recall seeing at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we see 65 ter 2070, please? Now, that picture really hasn't come out -- I have a better colour. It looks like we loaded this -- this got loaded in black and white somehow. With Madam Usher's assistance, if I could just place this on the ELMO? I see we are having some technical difficulties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Meek is stealing the show.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this piece of machinery?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is a ULT 220. It is a self-propelled construction machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, where were you, sir, when you first saw the ULT 220 arrive that day? Where do you remember being when you first saw it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By the water point. I was there when the machine arrived, this ULT 220.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And in this case, sir, was it driven by itself or did it come on a trailer?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By itself. It has rubber wheels and it moves by itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you had been told to expect this second piece of equipment that day?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know about it. No one told me about it. This machine arrived after some time, I don't know how much later, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did it go, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To another location.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Or to the other location.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: There were some people there were the public utility company. They loaded bodies on to the bucket and the machine would take them away.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did the machine take those bodies, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To the mass grave that had been dug out by the BGH-500.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the bodies that were loaded on to this ULT 220, which bodies were these, sir? Were these the bodies that you had described earlier encountering when you first arrived at this scene or were they other bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was at the other location. As for the group of killed people, the dispersed one, they were up there and I saw that some of them were uniformed and that others were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just try to clarify this in the couple of minutes that we have before the break. You say you saw members of the public utility company loading bodies. First of all, which public utility company are we talking about, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The public utility company of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you see them loading these bodies on to the ULT 220?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Once the ULT has arrived, they started loading the bodies, and then I went away. I went up to the school, and they continued their work by themselves. I did not return. And once they were done with it, they returned to their respective bases.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, the bodies that you saw the public utility workers loading on to the ULT, were those bodies bodies from the smaller group that you described seeing first or were they bodies from some other location or some other group?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was the other location, up there. Since the machine was first working at the other location.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Beyond the railroad tracks is what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, should we take the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We can take the break now. It will be of 25 minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you recall going back a few minutes ago when you were shown the photograph of the BGH digger. Do you recall the colour of the digger, sir, as you saw it on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall the colour of the ULT 220 that you saw on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Also yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, what was your reaction when you saw all of these bodies at the upper site?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, not pleasant, not comfortable.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Prior to travelling to that site, both near the water point and beyond the railroad, had you received any information, either overheard anyone speaking or heard anything, about executions taking place in Orahovac on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard in the unit that what had been done had to be buried, that people had to be buried up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, you told us earlier in your testimony that your reaction to receiving the order was, "Why me? Why do I have to go?" Was it your understanding that you were --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding that you were being sent to oversee the burial of people who had been executed?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They sent me to be by the machine in case something went wrong, in case one of the machines broke down, so I was there to intervene and they told me, "You have nothing to do with what's going on there." I did go there but I couldn't stand the sight very long, so I went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, based on your experience in the Engineering Company, what was your understanding of the relationship between the public utilities entity and the civil protection entity in the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The public utility company was established, we all knew why, and we knew what the public utility company's function was in the municipality. Now, as to why they sent those older people there to bury these other people, to collect them in the bucket and to carry them to the graves, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me just ask you this, sir: What is your understanding of what the civil protection people did in the Zvornik municipality? What was the purpose of civil protection?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, the civil protection, the word is self-explanatory. It's to provide assistance and help in case of fire, a natural disaster or similar things. People would gather to help other people in certain parts of town, in local communes, whereas the local utility company would be engaged in all sorts of municipal activities, collecting garbage, cleaning the town and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall who was operating these two machines when you were at the site near Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The BGH-500 was operated by Cvijetin Ristanovic, the machine operator, I believe. His profession was handling construction machinery. That was his position in the company where he had worked before the war and later on. As for the other machine, the ULT 220, which had come from the Glinica Birac company, was operated by somebody called Rade but I can't recall his family name.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. How long would you estimate you stayed at this location, whether it was near the water source or up near the railroad? How long did you stay in that general area?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I left earlier. I went on to -- on foot down to the school. A car came by from the line near Krizevici. The others remained to finish the job. And then they themselves retired to the base. But I don't know when that was. I don't know how late it was when they arrived. I believe that they worked until the dusk. The following day when I arrived at the unit, they told me that they had finished around 6.00 or 7.00 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, how long would you estimate you were in Orahovac on the 15th of July, from the time you arrived at the school to the time you left in that vehicle to return to the compound?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I could not stand the sight. That's why I went back to the school. There was an unpleasant scent in the air. And I must have spent about three or four hours in the whole area, walking to and fro the school and the water fountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you returned to your company, did you report to anyone, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I don't even remember whether anybody was in the office, whether Slavko was there or anybody else. I returned and then I went back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you remember speaking to anybody at the company compound about --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Before we move on, let's look at 65 ter 1705. Sir, do you see an image in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Take your time and get acquainted with it, and when you think you know or recognise what you're looking at, please just let us know and I'm going to ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see everything well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you just generally describe what this photograph depicts?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the place where the mass graves are, the two graves, the grave number 1 and the grave number 2. This is the road leading up to Krizevici.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can I just interrupt you for a second and ask Madam Usher to hand you the pen that I warned you might be coming. Would you mark with an X where the water source was that you stated was close to the road?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please draw a circle to indicate the area where you saw the first group of bodies that you told us about? And if you could just put a number 1 inside that circle for us, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you could draw another circle and indicate the area in which you say you saw the bodies dispersed, and if you could mark that area with a number 2, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, just place your initials on the area where you were standing when you came closest to seeing the bodies in area number 2.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would just write your initials there, please, there, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, just put today's date on the lower right-hand corner. And today is the 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think we can save this. And we are done with this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, at some point did you receive another assignment similar to the one that you were given on July 15th?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the following day, when I arrived at the unit, on the 16th, that was, I was again said to go to Kozluk for the same reason. What had been done had been done, and then they told Milos Mitrovic to take the small Skip there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And, sir, when you say what had been done had been done, please tell the Trial Chamber -- I know it might be difficult -- just tell the Trial Chamber what that means.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It means that people were executed at that location, and then I had to go subsequently to finish the job off, to bury the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall who gave you this order to go to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When I was at the unit, Slavko was there, Major Jokic was not there, he was not at the unit, and Sekonjic was there and an order came from Milos to go there with a small machine and for me to also go there to bury the bodies. They were in the crevices, in the field. Nothing had to be dug. Just the earth had to be put over the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get to that in just a few seconds, sir. Just one question. Where did this order to you and the order to Mr. Mitrovic originate, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe that Slavko sent Milos, Slavko Bogicevic sent Milos there. And I myself was told that I should also go there when I came in front of the office. I was told to be there as well. I was told that in the office. I don't know whether it was Slavko Bogicevic or Sekonjic, but one of them told me, "The major had told you to go there to finish the job off."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you travel to Kozluk by yourself, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was not alone. I was driven in a TAM lorry, TAM 75, which was a military vehicle. The driver drove me there, and then I proceeded on foot to the location because it was not easy to get to that location because of the stench that was spreading around.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall approximately what time you arrived at this location?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Around 8.00 or thereabouts, in the morning again.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please describe, as best as you can, what this area that you came to looked like, where was it located, what was the ground like when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was the location where the gravel was being dug for the construction industry. That's the kind of the terrain. There were holes in the ground from which gravels used to be excavated from, and all that was there. Somebody had also brought broken glass in one of the crevices there was broken glass. I believe that it had come from the Kozluk glass factory, the broken glass would be transported from the factory and unloaded in that same gravel field.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. You referred to a factory in Kozluk, sir. In fact, as you travelled to this area where the gravel pits were, did you have to pass any particular factory to get there?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By the Vitinka Kozluk mineral water plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is that the company to which you were just referring when, as I see it here on the transcript, it's referred to as the Kozluk glass factory?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. The factory produced mineral water and they probably used glass bottles to bottle the water, and when whatever glass got broken in the process would be deposited in those gravel pits, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you recall what colour the glass was that you saw, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The bottles would predominantly be either white or green. The white, however, prevailed. There was some green glass, however, but I didn't pay too much heed to the site. I just passed by that pit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And was this location close to a water source or a body of water?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity, maybe 20 or 30 metres away, is the bed of the Drina River.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, can you describe where you saw the bodies and the condition of the bodies, for the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Those gravel pits, on the surface, the bodies were decomposing. You couldn't stay for any longer. It was almost impossible to come any closer than maybe 20 metres. When I passed by that gravel pit containing glass, I hurried away. I couldn't stand the stench.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Could you tell what kind of clothing the bodies were clad in, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: During the short period of time that I spent by the gravel pits, I could see that there were some uniformed persons, and there were also bodies in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were these bodies, sir, already in the pits or were they on the surface of the ground?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All of them were in the pit. Just a few of them were on the surface. But it was all kind of close. The bodies were not scattered far away from the pits. They were all close to each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone else, other than Mr. Mitrovic and the driver, while you were at this site?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The driver who had brought me remained behind. Only Mitrovic came with this small Skip in order to bury the bodies and to prevent the stench from spreading. There may have been some three or four uniformed young men with normal belts, but they were masked. Their faces were painted. There was a group of some three or four of them. I did not approach them. I didn't ask them who they were. I couldn't recognise them. They were a bit further away from me and I wouldn't be able to tell you what they were doing there. Mitrovic could not do anything with his machine. His machine was very small, so that after a certain while, the ULT 220 arrived. This is a bigger machine. The driver got off his cabin. You could tell that he found the whole situation very difficult to sustain but he had to do it. I don't know whether he was under the pressure of these young men. And as I say, I don't know who they were, where they had come from. He had to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you order that ULT 220 to be brought to that location, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Who did, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that the order came from the unit. I suppose that they had realised that nothing could be done with the small machine, that that small machine was not fit for that job in that location, that it would take a very long time to accomplish the task, and I suppose that they had sent the big machine from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you know who was operating this ULT 220?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This machine belonged to the stone quarry in Josanica which is a company that quarried stone. This was their machine and the operator was Rade Boskovic. He was an employee of that company and he was the operator of that machine that belonged to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately how long you stayed at this site?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not long. Again, I left earlier. Milos left before me, with the small machine that was useless. Rade remained there after me. And then since he drove that self-propelling machine he returned in that machine once he had accomplished the job.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, did you leave before Mr. Boskovic finished the job or did you leave with him or did you leave after him?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I left before him.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you in fact see him operating his ULT 220, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I had to see that. He passed by me. He went there to finish whatever had to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And did you actually see him doing the job that he had been sent to do, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't in his immediate vicinity. I was a bit further off. But I did see him working.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And where did you go after you left this site in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I went to the unit. I got off the vehicle, and when I found no one in the office, I went back out in the street, I hitch-hiked and returned home and Rade returned to the base on his own.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, were you ordered a third time to go somewhere?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Every morning, whenever I came to the unit, I would be issued with tasks. Therefore, time came for the third day, when they told me to go to Branjevo. I asked what was I to do there and they said, "Well, the same job as the previous one awaits you." That's what they told me at the unit. Slavko and Sekonjic told me that, to go there immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you told to go anywhere in particular in Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In Branjevo, there was an execution by the farm, by the pig farm, in the area of Branjevo, and a pit was supposed to be dug out to dump the bodies in. I was told that the people from the utility company would come to load the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And were you already familiar with this farm in Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was not. Well, during the war, I would pass through that area on that road, via Branjevo, but I wasn't very familiar with the location itself, with the pig farm. I never went in there. I just passed by on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: How did you get there, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I got there in a small vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you drive yourself or did you have a driver?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. They sent a driver from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately what time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think it was past 8.00 or around 8.30, 9.00. It is rather far from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, was this in the morning or in the evening?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe what you saw when you arrived at the Branjevo Farm that morning?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, the vehicle stayed down the road, just before one is supposed to turn to the farm. I came to the farm itself and I encountered a group of workers from the farm. They were standing on the road. They told me -- well, they asked me whether anyone would come to do anything, and I said, "Yes, I guess so. I was sent up here." After that a BGH arrived on a trailer truck, after which a ULT arrived as well by itself. Whether any of the workers told them where to dig, I don't know, but I think it was supposed to be as far from the sties as possible. I didn't even have time to leave when they started digging, once the BGH arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, when you refer to workers from the farm, are you referring to civilian workers or military workers, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These were elderly civilians that were renting out the facilities and working on the farm, elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall seeing anyone from the rear battalion at that location?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the moment of my arrival, no one was there. However, later the elderly people from the public utilities company arrived to help with the whole thing, to get it over with.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what were these elderly people doing, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing at the moment of my arrival. They were standing within the perimeter, next to the sties.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then what did they do, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: They went to their own facilities. Occasionally they would come out of the buildings, just to see what was going on with the burial.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, did you see anyone other than the operator of the BGH or the operator of the ULT, who were operating their machines? Did you see anyone handle any of the bodies, do anything physically with any of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not at the moment of my arrival. I only saw those people from the farm, and later when I saw the machine operators.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Well, you said that the public utility people had been sent to help. What did they help do?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To load the bodies into the bucket. Sometimes the operator would pick up the bodies with the bucket itself, but mainly they were loaded on to it manually.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, are you aware that there was something known as the rear battalion in the Zvornik Brigade, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what was that rear battalion comprised of, in terms of the men in that battalion?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Predominantly, these were somewhat older people who were not supposed to go to the front lines, to the positions. They were in the rear, to do various tasks that had to be done. Usually elderly people or older.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall seeing any members of the rear battalion also working with the public utilities workers that day?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the group, when they arrived, there may have been two or three of them with them. I can't recall exactly. I can't recall any names. I didn't know any of them. But there was a group from the utilities company and perhaps two or three men from the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, did you stay at this site the entire time you were there, or did you go back and forth to some other location during this process of loading up the bodies and burying them?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was there almost up until the end, but not really close to them. I was next to the road and towards the outpatient clinic. It was supposed to cater for the Lokanj part of the area. I was closer to the road that was between the sties and the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you were at this clinic, did you speak with anybody or did you see anybody there that you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was there with a captain, a captain first class, I think, who was there at Lokanj. By profession he was a teacher. I can't recall his first or last name. He was an older person. His house was close to the clinic itself. I went up to see him and then we were standing by the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And can you describe anything about his appearance?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is an older man, somewhat stout. He had a belly. As far as I can recall what he looked like, he was rather heavily built.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall whether this captain was part of any particular battalion and, if so, do you recall to which brigade his battalion belonged?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was with the Lokanj Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately what time of the day it was when you left Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the evening, around 7.00 or 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you left, had the digging and burying been completed or was it still going on?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Some bodies remained. I left, and once they were done, the self-propelling machine went on its own. The other one was loaded on to the truck, and sent to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we may have P02103 on e-court, please, and specifically page 210. Actually, may we have page 212, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have page 212, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this location in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what it is, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's the Branjevo Farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: You mentioned some pigsties, sir. I just ask to you take that pen and you may require some assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you just please draw an X on the pigsties that you recall?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks] Over here, in this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you refer to "this part," are you referring to the two long buildings with the red roofs, sir, as being the pigsties?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you see the area in this photograph where the bodies were being buried?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Should I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If you can, if you can draw a circle in the area where the bodies were being buried.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: All right, sir. I'd just ask you to place your initials on the lower right-hand corner and today's date, the 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can save it. And we'll be done with this exhibit. And when we are done, if we could have page 210 up, please? Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: First question, sir, do you read English?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just ask you to look at this and can you tell us what this overhead image represents?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is the same location at Branjevo as shown in the previous photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if you would, please mark with Xs the pigsties.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, just draw a line to indicate the area in which this digging and burying was going on. If you can do it with a circle, fine but if it's just easier to draw a line to show the extent of the area that you recall seeing.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is this part here. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If you would just again place your initials in the lower right-hand corner and today's date, the 29th of August.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: We can save this and we'll move on from this exhibit. Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you ever speak to Major Jokic, your chief of engineering, about these assignments that you received?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I did. Whenever we met. We didn't meet daily but on occasion. I would ask him about it and he said, "Well, someone had to do it. Since you were there with your men, from the road and bridge platoon, you were tasked with that, since you know how to work in the field. That's why you were sent."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, based on what you were seeing and hearing over these days when you had these assignments, were these executions a secret in your company? Or was it something people were talking about and knew about?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Before the whole thing, I spent two or three days at home getting ready to see my son off to serve his military term. I didn't know about the whole thing. Once I returned to the unit, it was then that I was told what I was supposed to do. Before that, I had no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And these assignments that you received to bury the bodies of these people who had been executed, were they a secret in your company?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. It was no secret at all. All of the people in the company knew that it had to be done. The soldiers talked about it between themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on each of these days when you were sent to these three locations, were you the highest-ranking member of your company at those sites?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was, but the soldiers were the operators. Since I was a staff sergeant from the times before the war, I was assigned to accompany them. That was my task within the company, to carry out such tasks and to command the road and bridges platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And is it your testimony that you did not issue a single order to any of your men in connection with these three assignments?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "No" what? "No," you didn't issue a single order or, "No," this is not your testimony? What we want to know from you very clearly, Mr. Lazarevic, is: Did you on occasion at any time issue a single order to any of your men in connection with these three assignments? What's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not, not to anyone. I never issued a specific task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that clear, Mr. Thayer?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever mark any of the sites with pegs or in any fashion prior to the bodies being buried at any of them?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not me. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you ever show anyone at any of these sites where to bury the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Did you become aware at any time after these events of any operation to dig up all those bodies and rebury them elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After the initial burial, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When did you hear about it, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: After some time. I don't know how much later exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you have any information or knowledge about your Engineering Company being involved in any way in such activities?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you share that information for us, please? What information do you have of your Engineering Company being involved in any way with the reburial of these bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I heard that the machine operators went somewhere. The ones who did the initial burying were called in to dig the bodies out.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir -- I'm sorry, please continue.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was assigned to do that the same way it was done the first time, from the engineering base. I was told to go there with them when they begin working, they made a list of men. Major Jokic and Slavko Bogicevic did that. They were the people who were supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall when you were given this assignment, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was at home. I was on furlough on that day. I was off duty. They called me on the phone. Slavko Bogicevic called me. And told me to come urgently. I went there. He was standing in front of the barracks. He handed me a piece of paper. I asked him what that was. And he explained to me that the bodies had to be dug out and transferred somewhere, and he also handed me the list of people who were supposed to go with me. Again I asked, "Why me?" But it turned out that the major actually decided that he should go with that group of people. He didn't want to do that. And instead of going himself, he called me at home and when I got there, he gave me that list and told me what to do and what had been prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And this is Major Jokic, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Major Jokic and Slavko Bogicevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, do you recall approximately what month this occurred, this assignment to dig up the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know when, what month. I don't know the date. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Was it in 1995, sir, before the end of the -- before December of 1995?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It was in 1995, but I don't know what month.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, did you, in the end, personally participate in any way in this reburial -- or digging up and reburial of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I participated in the same way as before. I was there, but I was not in the immediate vicinity of the site. The people who were doing the reburial knew what to do, and they did it on their own. They were the ones who dug the bodies out and did the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of the locations that you went to during this reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I went to the same locations where the bodies were originally buried. That was my task. My task was to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And on any of these occasions, did you follow the bodies to the locations where they were to be reburied?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to review some more documents with you. The first is 65 ter number 297. Now, sir, with Madam Usher's assistance, I want to show you an original document, original item. Sir, if you would, just pick up that book, feel free to pick it up. Would you just leaf through it and tell us if you recognise what it is?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is the book where daily orders and tasks of the Engineering Company were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could go to page 135 in the original B/C/S, and that's page 15 in the English, and, sir, that's page 126 of the original there. If you're looking at the logbook, in the upper right-hand corner it's page 126. Sir, can you read what the first line of that page 126 says?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The duty officer in the company command on 15 July 1995 will be Sergeant First Class Damjan Lazarevic."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And at the very top of that page, sir, what does it say? What's the very first line on the page?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Daily order of the company commander for 15 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you recall what the purpose of this logbook was?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
