utterances.text: It showed who the duty officer in the company was, what people were supposed to do, what they did, on certain days. I was assigned as the duty officer in the company on the day when I was sent to Krizevici, to Orahovac. I was not even in the company. The common practice was if somebody was sent away to the field, then somebody else would act as the duty officer, and it could have even been a foot soldier. It did not necessarily have to be an officer. That was a common practice in the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And who do you recall being responsible for writing in this information every day?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The company officer did it most of the time. If he wasn't there, then it would be the deputy company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "company officer," to whom are you referring specifically, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The person who recorded daily orders. If he wasn't there, then it would be Slavko Bogicevic the deputy commander or if even he wasn't there then it would be the company commander himself who would make a record of the things that people are supposed to do on a certain day.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I'm sorry, I asked an unclear question. What was the name of the company officer? I think you may have referred to him as the desk officer.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Sekonjic, Vojislav, Vojkan Sekonjic. I believe that his name is Vojkan, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, I want to turn your attention to numbers 4, 5, 6 and 7 on this page under the heading of "tasks." Again, that's on the 15th of July, page 126, the page -- if you just turn to page 126, the page you just had, or if you want to look at your computer, do you see under "tasks", sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: What does number 4 say?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "BGH-700 to work in Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next line, number 5, task number 5, what does that say?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The ULT 220 to work in Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next line, number 6?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The ULT to work in Petkovci." I don't know anything about this. I don't know anything about bullet number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. How about bullet number 7? What does that say, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, I know nothing about the bullet number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That is working with the excavator at Petkovci, you don't know anything about that, correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Correct, I don't know. I know nothing about the bullet number 6 or 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. May we look at the next page of this document? And, sir, if you want to just look at the next page, page 127, no, I don't think you need to turn the page. I think you'll see that it's right there. And what does the first line there say, sir, at the very top of the page?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Daily order by the company commander for 16 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you would, would you just read task number 2 and task number 3?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Working with the BGH-700 in Orahovac." And number 3: "Working with ULT 220 in Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we may look at the next page of the document, please? And sir, if you just turn the page to page 128, as it's marked there. What does the first line say on this page, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Daily order by company commander for 17 July 1995."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please read entries -- first entry number 2?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Working with BGH-700 in Branjevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next item, the next task, number 3, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Working with ULT 220 in Branjevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And task number 5, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "BGH-700 should be transported to Branjevo."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And does it indicate how? By what means?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't indicate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay, sir, you can close that. And thank you. I want to show you a couple of more documents, sir. If we could look at 65 ter number 301. And with Madam Usher's assistance, I'm going to hand you the original because it may be more legible for you. And actually, we need the next page, because I think this was ERNed backwards but I'll -- Sir -- and if we could just scroll to the top of the document. There is something in handwriting at the top of the page on the right-hand side, and it seems to be underlined. What does that say, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Birac holding," the aluminum factory in Birac, Birac Holding.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we could just scroll down? That's fine actually. There appears to be a line with a date range of July 1st to 31st, 1995. What does that line indicate, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. We have the original there. There is -- there is a line with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can someone point to the line with the pointer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, if you look back at your computer, can you see the line that's being shown to you? I know it's a little difficult?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Backhoe excavator, Torpedo."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, right above that line, sir, what does that line indicate, the line above the line that says --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Yes. What does that line indicate, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 1st of July to 31st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And the second line, as you've just read it, underneath that? What is the second -- the line directly underneath that date indicate? There is something in Cyrillic and then something typewritten. Could you just read that, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't see a thing on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If would you look at the original, then, just hold it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Right above that line, and you read part of it a moment ago, what does that line say? Can you read the Cyrillic and then the typewritten line after it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What I've read was, "Backhoe excavator, Torpedo." What else should I read?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is this document, sir? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what this document is?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a travel and work logbook which existed for every construction vehicle or every piece of construction equipment that we had in our possession.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And we've already explained what Rovokopac is. What is "Torpedo"? Is that just a brand name of a digger?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that it was its brand name. It was also a smaller machine looking like a tractor, with a small bucket in the front and a somewhat bigger digging basket in the back for digging holes, and I suppose that Torpedo is the make of that machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if you can just look a little further down on this document, there are two names that appear. Can you read those, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Cvijetin Ristanovic and Milos Mitrovic. These two names mean that there was one machine and two operators. They would take turns. For example, one would work for two or three days and then he would be off for two days and the other would take over. Both names are here to indicate who was the one who filled the tank with fuel. In any case, these two people operated one machine. One machine, two operators, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: If we could just look down a little further, there is a larger chart, and on the first column on the left side, there appear to be some dates. Do you see the chart, sir, and there are some dates? Thank you, thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the 11th, the 14th, the 16th, the 21st, and in the last line, 23rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what do the two lines for the 14th and the 16th indicate to you, as you read the information going from left to right, let's start with the entry for the 14th of July. What does that entry say?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The date, and then there is the number of the travel order, and then after that the quantity of fuel issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: In litres, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In litres, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And then going all the way across to the far right of the chart, what's that last column, sir? What does that indicate?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are signatures, the signatures of somebody from the rear, confirming how much fuel had been issued and used for whatever work was done with the machine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, if we could go to the other page of this document, please? And again, sir, if it helps you to look at the original, please do so. We'll have it up on the screen and just feel free to use whichever one is more legible. Again, on the far left, we have a column that appears to have dates on it. Just generally speaking, sir, without looking at any particular entry, what is this page designed to communicate? What's the information on this page supposed to tell the reader?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a -- the description of every particular day of where the machines were sent, which route they took. For example on the 11th of July 1995, the Republika Srpska army. It says, "The base," and I can't decipher the next word.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: That's okay, sir. We are going to be talking about a couple of the other ones in particular. But if you look at column number 16, as we move across the document from left to right, what does that indicate, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: These are vehicle hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. The number of hours that the vehicle was in use; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The number of hours that the machine was used according to the travel order or the work order.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we could swing back to the far left of the document, sir, I just want you to read, please, the entire entry for -- do you see a date of 14 July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The base-Orahovac-the base, digging trenches in Orahovac."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the time there? Vehicle time? Use time?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Five hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, if we could look at the next entry underneath that one, underneath the entry for the 14th of July, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The base-Orahovac-the base, digging trenches in Kozluk."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir, I just want to make sure we have read the right line. If you could look at -- see the entry for the 16th, and just move slowly to the right under column 4. Can you read what it says there for the entry on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The base-Kozluk-the base. Digging trenches in Kozluk."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the time if you can see it there on the original, the time spent?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Eight, eight hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just to go back to column 2, what does that column indicate for those dates on the 14th and the 16th, column 2?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "The base-Orahovac-the base" on the 14th and on the 16th, "The base-Kozluk-the base."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, now if you're looking at the column number 2 -- Do you see that, there sir, as you're moving left to right, columns 1 through 20, I'm asking you about column 2?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Indication" -- yes, I can see the VRS, the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And that's the case for the 14th and the 16th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think so. I believe that the same applies because no other indication has been put.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm sorry, please finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But these two machines, on those two days, on the 16th, it did go to Kozluk but it did not do anything. And on the 14th, this particular machine was not up there. It was not in Orahovac. The other one, the bigger one, the BGH-500, was there. Somebody just put this information randomly. When I arrived in Orahovac, a BGH was there. The Torpedo wasn't there. The Torpedo was in Kozluk. Milos Mitrovic took him there but it was useless. He could not do anything with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it's time for a break and we just have a couple more documents to review with the witness when we return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm handing to Madam Registrar the clean copy of what you handed to us earlier on, indicating the parts that you need to redact. What is not cancelled on the sheet that I'm handing to you must not be redacted. Just give it to Mr. Thayer. Then we'll verify it, Mr. Zivanovic, later on, and you will have the newly redacted copy. Thank you. We will have a 25-minute break, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May we have 65 ter number 302, please? And may I have the assistance of Madam Usher?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay, sir. Do you see a document on the computer in front of you? And I've also given you the original of that document, if that's easier for you to read. Okay. There is a typewritten line at the very top of the document, just above that series of numbers. Can you read what that typewriting says at the very top of the document, sir, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Construction machine, the property of the Birac Holding company."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And just looking a little further down the document, what is the date range again for this piece of equipment?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From the 1st of July until the 31st of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And what is this piece of equipment from Birac Holding, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Construction machine ULT 220, four wheels, self-propelled, colour yellow.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And there is a name that appears in the small chart just a little further down. Do you know -- can you read that and can you tell the Trial Chamber who that person is?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's the name of the operator of that piece of equipment. He used to work at the holding, at the Birac Holding company. His name was Veljko Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And proceeding down a little further into the larger chart, do you see some entries for the dates of July 15th and July 17th, in terms of the fuel that was used?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the 15th of July, 60 litres of fuel was put in. On the 17th of July, 100 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And do you see two other entries also for the 15th and the 17th, in that same column, and if so, what are the fueling amounts there?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 15th, 40 litres, the 17th, 70 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, if we may have the second page of this document shown on e-court, please? And, sir, I couldn't tell -- if you could turn the page over, if you could look at the back of the document? Okay. And in column 1, do you see two dates, sir? One underneath the other?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 17th of July 1995, VRS, digging trenches in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Just ask you to take another look, if you would, under column 1, if you could look at the date on the very first entry there, right under column 1 where it says the date. Can you take a look and tell us what that date is for that first entry?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 15th of July 1995, VRS, digging of trenches in Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how many hours does this log indicate this ULT 220 worked on that day at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here 5.00.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Five hours.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: But it should have been longer. But someone wrote down five hours only. I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And looking down at that second entry, if we could scroll all the way to the left, thank you, what is the second date under column 1, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 17th of July 1995, VRS, digging trenches in Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how much time was spent at Branjevo, according to this log?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here eight and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: May we have 65 ter number 299 on e-court, please? And again, sir, I'm going to show you the original with the assistance of Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could I make a correction as to the other date?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Certainly, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This machine was not at Branjevo on the 17th. There was another machine there. It was also a ULT 220 but it was the property of the quarry at Josanica, not this one. I know it for certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. And the fuel that was used to refuel these vehicles, where was -- where was that done and whose fuel was it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The VRS, our brigade, at the gas station. That's where our vehicles were filled with fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. This is the last document I'm going to show you, sir. And again, what's the date range for this vehicle? If you could look at the front, page. Thank you, sir. Do you have -- do you see the image on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can't see it. I can see the original much better.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Great. Thank you, sir. Then if you would, please read the date range on this document.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is not a construction machine. This is a truck, a vehicle, 2626 D2. It is a truck used to transport material.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the manufacturer of this truck, if you can read it, sir? What's the word right before 2626?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What's the make of the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says here D2, type of fuel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's the line before, above that. What's the make? You've told us that this was a truck, a 2626, or whatever the number is, but what make was the truck?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A Mercedes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, again, there is a name a little lower down. Can you read that? And do you know who that person is?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I do. Milan Milovanovic. He used to be a driver in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And if we go down to that larger chart, if we could just scroll down a little bit, there are some entries for the 14th and 17th of July. Do you see those there, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July, 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how much fuel was --

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 30 litres. On the 17th of July, it was 30 litres as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, from your recollection, sir, if a vehicle was requisitioned from an outside company like the Glinica or Birac Holding as you've referred to it, would that company be responsible for fueling the vehicle or would it be VRS, in this case, Zvornik Brigade, fuel that would be used to keep that vehicle going and to -- and refueled?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Predominantly the vehicles would be provided with fuel by the brigade. However, if the brigade was short of fuel, then they were supposed to be provided fuel for by the companies from which they were requisitioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to the next page, please, sir, and I just have a few more questions on this document for you. If we could scroll up just a little bit, and, sir, going down column 1 all the way on the left, do you see an entry for the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And would you please just read across this entry and tell us what it says?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 14th of July 1995, "The base at Krizevici, transport of an excavator on a trailer."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, does it say "base at Krizevici" or "base to Krizevici", sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The reference is made to the engineering base, to Krizevici and back to the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. If would you just look down to the very next row, at the entry for the 16th of July, and if you would just read that entry all the way across, please, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 16th of July, 1995, "Base to Orahovac, transport of excavator and trailer."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And the next entry at July 17th, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 17th of July, 1995, "Base to Standard," which is where the seat of our brigade was, "To Branjevo, to base. Transport of BGH-700."

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, just continuing to go to the right on that line, if we could scroll over a little bit, do you recognise the signature there on that particular entry on the 17th of July?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The 17th, it is my signature. I signed this. Someone was supposed to sign. When I was present, I would. If I was absent, it would be signed by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. I think we are done with these documents. Now, sir, I just want to ask you some additional questions about the reburial of these bodies. You referred to a list of people that had been compiled and shown to you, of people that, I believe, were supposed to work, people that belonged to your company, during this operation. Do you know who compiled that list, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From my company, two or rather three operators were singled out. The rest were from other units, not from the engineering unit. There were only three of our men from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say "unit," sir, are you referring to other units or battalions of the Zvornik Brigade or are you talking about other brigades?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I mean other units. From my unit, from the engineering unit, there were only three men. The rest were from the Zvornik Brigade, from its different units.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Were you ever shown a map of the locations where these bodies were going to be reburied, sir? Or did you ever hear of such a map?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, never. No one has ever shown me such a map, and I don't know of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you aware of or did you receive any information about who chose these reburial locations?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: When you were at these same three sites, when the bodies were being dug up, were you there when the vehicles that were used to transport those corpses arrived to take them away, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I was. I was there when they arrived, and when those people started loading, but not too close. However, I was in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe what kind of vehicles were used to transport those bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The vehicles of the company, trucks from various companies. Our vehicles were old, and we couldn't use them to complete the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And how often do you recall those trucks having to arrive to transport those corpses from these various locations, sir, to be reburied?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Whenever needed at each of the locations; whenever needed they would arrive there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Are you able to even estimate how many times at these locations these trucks arrived, sir, to take away these bodies?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know how many times each of the vehicles came, but they were present at all three locations when there was a reburial.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, was this during the day or during the night?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you describe what it was like for you, in terms of the smell, as these bodies were being dug up and placed on these trucks?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was unbearable. The machine operators would abandon their vehicles in order to get some air. They couldn't stand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did the brigade receive any assistance from any other brigades or units, for example, the 5th Engineers, or any corps level or higher level units, in carrying out this operation?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I know, we did the digging out. As to who subsequently reburied the bodies, I don't know. We weren't able to know. And we weren't told either. I don't know where the load was taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: So, sir, then is it your testimony that as far as you knew, Zvornik Brigade Engineering Company members were not tasked to help bury those bodies wherever they may have been buried? I should say should rebury those bodies, wherever they had been reburied.

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's clarify this now because as put, it may lead to -- leave some doubt. You are confirming to us, Mr. Lazarevic, that the Zvornik Brigade Engineering Company was not tasked with the reburying, reburial, of any of these bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, sir, to your knowledge, from what you were told at the time or from what you heard later on, were there other burial sites that were exhumed, unearthed, at which this operation occurred, in addition to the three that you were involved with, did you ever become aware that that was done elsewhere, where other mass executions and burials occurred?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. I'm not aware of it. I know the three locations, our locations in the area of Zvornik, and the people buried and then reburied. As for any other locations, I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Can you estimate approximately how many days this reburial operation that occurred in the Zvornik Brigade zone of responsibility took?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe five or six days at the most. This is how long it went on for. If we are talking about the three locations in the area of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: At any of these locations, when you were present, was there anyone of a higher rank or authority than yourself?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While I was present there with the soldiers, nobody else came. I did not see anybody. However, I wasn't there all the time, while all this was being done, I would pop by for a moment and stayed there just for a short while, but then I would leave, I would go as far away as possible because I just couldn't stand the stench.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Now, given that this process, this operation, took several days, can you tell the Trial Chamber where you recall all of the fuel that would have been needed for this operation coming from?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: From the brigade, from the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: From what you saw, from what you had been told by Mr. Bogicevic or perhaps by Major Jokic, did this operation appear to you to be coordinated solely by the Zvornik Brigade or by some higher level command, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, that calls -- it's leading and a suggestive question. It calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Right. You can rephrase the question. The way you put it, it's marginal. Mr. Meek may be right. So I would suggest you rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you were there. Based on what you saw, based on what you were told by the people within your command, did it appear that this operation was something that was coordinated entirely by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Same objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me consult with my colleagues, now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The reason why I asked you to rephrase the question in the first place is because you could have put a very direct question. To your knowledge, or do you know who coordinated this whole operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, can you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Major Trbic, who was in the Zvornik Brigade. He was up there in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir, who is Major Trbic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: He was up there in the brigade. He was a major in charge of security, I believe. I don't know. But I believe that he was in charge of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, sir, what is the basis of your answer that it was Major Trbic in the Zvornik Brigade who coordinated this operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, I believe that question also misstates the evidence. The witness just said Major Trbic was in the command. This witness also, Your Honour, has already testified in the last ten minutes that no one told him anything about this situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop, stop. I mean, there is a limit beyond which you shouldn't go. The reference to the Zvornik Brigade, I think Mr. Meek is right, because the -- not completely because actually the previous answer was, "He was up there in the brigade. He was a major in charge of security." The only thing is that on line 23 on the previous page, he said, "Major Trbic, who was in the Zvornik Brigade. He was up there in the command." That's the only thing, but you can clarify this and you have also not asked him for the first name of this so-called Major Trbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, just a couple of questions to clarify. First you heard Mr. President's question. Do you recall the first name of this Major Trbic?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Nothing comes to mind, but I know the man. He was from our brigade. I can't remember off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when you say he was "up at the command," what do you mean, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the command. He was in charge of all these reburial and transfer of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Which command, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: At the command of the Zvornik Brigade. He was up there, and people addressed him as to what to do and how.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And again, sir, what is the basis of your testimony that it was this Major Trbic at the command of the Zvornik Brigade who coordinated this reburial operation?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because, after every job, he would summon us up there to inquire as to what had been done, how much had been done. That's how I know. I never spoke to anybody else. Nobody else called me to report to him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With the Court's indulgence, may I just have a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, just two more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, did you know at the time who Mr. or Major Trbic's superior was in the command?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Drago Nikolic. He was in charge of security, him and Trbic both.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And sir, do you recall whether or not you told the investigator in Banja Luka in 2002, when you met for your interview, any of this information about the reburial operation? Do you recall whether at the time you mentioned any of this information to him?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, he did ask me questions, but at the moment I did not provide any answers to him about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And when do you recall first telling any investigator or anybody about this reburial operation and the people that were involved in it and your role in it?

utterances.speaker: DAMJAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I did not. Nobody ever asked me as to what, when, why. Nobody ever asked me about that. If they had asked me, I would have told them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question before we adjourn, because I suppose no one would like to start the cross-examination at this late hour. Mr. Lazarevic, during the days when you were called to go to Orahovac and Kozluk, did you meet or see or speak to Major Trbic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're talking about the initial burials, the first time around?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Only the second time around, during the exhumation operations, he was my superior for that operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. We will continue tomorrow afternoon, Mr. Lazarevic, when the cross-examinations will start. In the meantime, I need to tell you that between now and tomorrow, when you continue with your evidence, you're not to discuss or talk to anyone in connection with the subject matter of your testimony. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Thank you, everybody. We'll reconvene tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
